findings.title: CIMA AML/CFT/CPF Rule and Financial Sanctions Rule take effect September 18, 2026
findings.summary: On 20 July 2026, CIMA published two finalised Rules carrying the force of law, effective 18 September 2026: the Rule on Effective Compliance Programme for the Prevention and Detection of Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Proliferation Financing for Financial Services Providers, and the Rule on Compliance with Financial Sanctions and Targeted Financial Sanctions. The Rules apply to all CIMA-registered or licensed entities including private funds and mutual funds. New obligations include mandatory independent AML audit cycles, enhanced outsourcing oversight, real-time sanctions screening, governance structure requirements (AMLCO, MLRO, DMLRO designations), and fund-level risk assessments — compliance must be completed before 18 September 2026.

findings.title: Cayman CRS Compliance Form deadline September 15, 2026
findings.summary: For the 2025 reporting year (filed in 2026), the Cayman Islands Compliance Form deadline under the Common Reporting Standard is September 15, 2026. The CRS Return itself was due July 31, 2026. By mid-2026, home tax authorities across 100+ CRS partner jurisdictions are receiving full 2025 financial account data, meaning non-compliance is more detectable than ever.

findings.title: Cyprus Pillar Two public consultation closed September 5, 2026; amendments to align with OECD and EC
findings.summary: The Cyprus Ministry of Finance opened a public consultation on 30 July 2026 on amendments to the Global Minimum Level of Taxation Law, prepared in response to European Commission observations on transposition of Council Directive (EU) 2022/2523. The consultation closed 5 September 2026. The proposed amendments aim to align Cyprus domestic rules with OECD guidance ahead of the Republic's autumn 2026 assessment. Cyprus also separately adopted additional Pillar Two guidance confirming entry-into-force dates for Side-by-Side package safe harbors, and the European Commission confirmed qualified status of Cyprus' Income Inclusion Rule.

findings.title: FinCEN final rule effective August 14, 2026: U.S. companies fully exempt from BOI reporting; only foreign-formed entities registered in the US remain as reporting companies
findings.summary: FinCEN published a final rule in the Federal Register on August 14, 2026, permanently removing the requirement for all U.S.-formed entities and their beneficial owners to report beneficial ownership information under the Corporate Transparency Act. All domestic reporting companies are now exempt. Only entities formed under the law of a foreign country and registered to do business in any U.S. State or Tribal jurisdiction remain as 'reporting companies.' FinCEN also announced it will delete previously reported BOI submitted by U.S. persons from its database. This is a significant rollback from the prior rule.

findings.title: MAS announced August 19, 2026 package to strengthen Singapore as asset management hub: tax exemption on performance fees, Hedge Fund Investment Programme, ONE Pass track
findings.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore announced on 19 August 2026 a three-part measure: (1) a new tax exemption for profit-related returns (performance/carry) on fund management services to qualifying funds, expected to apply from Year of Assessment 2027; (2) a new Hedge Fund Investment Programme under which MAS will invest directly with hedge fund managers committing to establish or expand Singapore presence; and (3) a new Investment Management Track under the ONE Pass framework recognising investment-performance-linked compensation for talent visa eligibility. These measures signal Singapore's bid to compete with London and Hong Kong for fund manager domicile.

findings.title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) permanently raises US estate/gift/GST exemption to $15 million per person effective January 1, 2026
findings.summary: Congress enacted the OBBBA, preventing the sunset of enhanced estate, gift, and generation-skipping transfer (GST) tax exemptions and permanently raising the per-person exemption to $15 million ($30 million per married couple with portability), indexed for inflation from 2027. The annual gift tax exclusion remains $19,000 ($38,000 per couple). The act also permanently suspends miscellaneous itemized deductions (including investment management fees) and caps itemized deductions at 35% for those in the top bracket. This removes the major planning urgency around the prior 2025 sunset cliff.

findings.title: Luxembourg transposes DAC9 and operationalises Pillar Two online filing; first GIR exchanges occur December 31, 2026
findings.summary: On December 17, 2025, Luxembourg Parliament approved Bill 8591 transposing EU Directive 2025/872 (DAC9) and amending the Pillar Two Law, with online registration via MyGuichet.lu operational since January 8, 2026. First GloBE Information Return (GIR) filings for calendar-year entities were due June 30, 2026. The first international exchanges of GIR data — for tax years starting on or after December 31, 2023 — will occur on December 31, 2026. Luxembourg also introduced a new tax credit for investments in young innovative companies (20% credit on ≥€10,000 qualifying investments) and increased pension savings deduction to €4,500/year.

findings.title: Trusts (Jersey) Amendment Law 2026 in force March 20, 2026: sole-trustee resignation, beneficiary termination, lender priority
findings.summary: The eighth amendment to the Trusts (Jersey) Law 1984 came into force on 20 March 2026, introducing three key changes: (1) a sole trustee cannot resign without appointing a successor; (2) the rule in Saunders v Vautier does not apply where a power to add beneficiaries exists, preventing beneficiaries from compelling trust termination; and (3) a lender's secured interest takes priority over a trustee's or former trustee's lien over trust assets, unless otherwise agreed. The changes provide enhanced certainty for trust financing transactions and protect settlor intentions against beneficiary-driven termination.

findings.title: Guernsey trust law amendments passed May 2026; all private trust companies must now hold fiduciary licence or limited permission
findings.summary: Guernsey's legislature passed amendments to the Trusts (Guernsey) Law 2007 on 20 May 2026, clarifying existing statutory provisions and resolving ambiguities highlighted by recent case law. Separately, the Guernsey Financial Services Commission updated its guidance in September 2025 requiring all private trust companies (PTCs) — previously exempt — to obtain either a full fiduciary licence under section 6 of the Fiduciaries Law or a 'limited permission' under section 3(1)(ac), effective immediately for new PTCs and requiring remediation for existing ones. The PTC must be administered within the AML controls of a licensed fiduciary.

findings.title: BVI legitimate interest access to beneficial ownership registry live since April 1, 2026; 25% ownership threshold applies
findings.summary: From 1 April 2026, the BVI Financial Services Commission began accepting applications from persons demonstrating legitimate interest to access beneficial ownership information in the statutory registry. Access is available under a 25% ownership or control threshold. Entities that missed the January 1, 2026 filing deadline are marked 'In Penalty'; a moratorium on fees and penalties ran until March 31, 2026. The new regime replaced the legacy BOSS system following the January 2, 2025 transition to the statutory beneficial ownership framework under amended BVI Business Companies Act.

findings.title: Switzerland extends CRS 2.0 / CARF automatic exchange of information to crypto-assets effective 2026
findings.summary: Switzerland's implementation of CRS 2.0 and the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) took effect from January 2026, extending automatic exchange of financial account information to crypto-asset holdings. Swiss financial institutions and crypto platforms must now report qualifying crypto account data for automatic exchange with partner jurisdictions. From 2027, Swiss and French (and Italian) tax authorities will also begin exchanging 2026 salary data of cross-border employees. Canton-level wealth tax on crypto holdings continues to apply to all private crypto investors.

findings.title: BCB VASP authorization deadline October 30, 2026; grandfathered firms must apply by then or face enforcement
findings.summary: Brazil's Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) Resolutions 519, 520, and 521 (November 2025) operationalised the 2022 Virtual Assets Law, creating the Sociedades Prestadoras de Serviços de Ativos Virtuais (SPSAV) licensing regime. The regime entered into force on February 2, 2026. Pre-existing VASPs operating before that date have a 270-day grandfathering period to apply for formal BCB authorization, making the deadline October 30, 2026. Unauthorized firms face enforcement. Authorization requires capital between R$10.8M and R$37.2M, robust AML/CFT controls, and public transparency.

findings.title: Federal Decree-Law No. 10 of 2025 establishes comprehensive UAE AML/CFT/CPF framework; mandatory goAML registration and enhanced KYC platform in force through 2026
findings.summary: Federal Decree-Law No. 10 of 2025 (issued September 30, 2025), comprising 71 articles and nearly 300 enforceable requirements, established the UAE's most comprehensive AML/CFT/CPF framework to date. All regulated entities must register on the goAML platform and file reports regardless of whether any suspicious transactions have occurred. Federal Decree-Law No. 30 of 2024 created a digital KYC platform for collecting, analysing, and exchanging KYC data across entities. In 2026, UAE authorities have increased inspections and enforcement actions; the DFSA's regulated population grew 14% in 2024 to over 900 firms, including a 75% increase in wealth management licences.

findings.title: USA formally exempt from Pillar Two; Belgium extended GIR notification to September 30, 2026; over 60 jurisdictions implementing
findings.summary: In January 2026, the US Department of the Treasury announced that US-headquartered multinational groups will be exempt from Pillar Two's requirements, and the US will not implement GloBE rules. Over 60 jurisdictions have enacted or are actively implementing GloBE rules as of mid-2026. Belgium extended its GIR notification form deadline (for FY2024) from June 30, 2026 to September 30, 2026. The OECD's Side-by-Side package continues to coordinate compliance obligations globally. The first OECD GIR filing deadline for calendar-year taxpayers was June 30, 2026 in most jurisdictions.
findings.source_name: OECDPillars.com / PwC Pillar Two Country Tracker

findings.title: Panama SBP Rule 1-2026 mandates enhanced AML documentation for bank onboarding; Draft Law 314 introduces fintech licensing
findings.summary: Panama's Superintendencia de Bancos (SBP) Rule 1-2026 prescribes a structured documentary pack banks must collect before onboarding any business client, with enhanced obligations for higher-risk entities including fintechs and virtual-asset businesses. Required documents include a beneficial-ownership declaration to the ultimate natural person and an AML/CTF policy manual aligned with SBP Rule 1-2026. Draft Law 314, currently advancing, would introduce a purpose-built licensing regime for crypto exchanges, token custodians, and payment aggregators. Panama was removed from the FATF grey list in 2023 and the EU high-risk list in 2025, reducing investor friction.

findings.title: Cyprus 8% flat crypto tax (Article 20E) effective January 1, 2026; corporate income tax raised to 15%
findings.summary: From 1 January 2026, Cyprus applies a single 8% flat tax rate to virtually all forms of crypto-asset disposals and income under new Article 20E of the Income Tax Law, replacing the previously ambiguous treatment. Separately, Cyprus raised its corporate income tax rate from 12.5% to 15% effective January 1, 2026, to comply with the EU Pillar Two Directive minimum rate requirements. Cyprus retains zero tax on capital gains (except Cyprus real estate), no wealth tax, no inheritance tax, and no gift tax, preserving its attractiveness for wealth structures.

findings.title: Florida SB 264 restrictions on foreign real estate buyers upheld by 11th Circuit; FIRPTA 15% withholding continues
findings.summary: In November 2025, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit upheld Florida's Senate Bill 264 (effective July 1, 2023), which significantly restricts real estate purchases by nationals of seven designated 'countries of concern' (China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Venezuela, Syria). Chinese nationals face a near-total ban; other designated-country nationals face restrictions primarily near military and critical infrastructure. All buyers must sign an affidavit confirming compliance; violations risk forfeiture and criminal charges. FIRPTA withholding remains at 15% of gross sale price. No new legislation affecting foreign buyers passed in Florida in 2026.

findings.title: CRS 2.0 and DAC8 (EU) effective January 2026: crypto-assets now subject to automatic information exchange
findings.summary: CRS 2.0, the first major update to the Common Reporting Standard since 2016, took effect in January 2026, expanding reportable assets to include crypto-assets and strengthening due diligence requirements. Simultaneously, EU Directive DAC8 came into force in January 2026, aligning EU rules with the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) and closing the tax transparency gap created by digital assets. Financial institutions and crypto-asset service providers in CRS/DAC8 jurisdictions must now collect and report client crypto holdings. The Cayman Islands Compliance Form deadline under CRS is September 15, 2026.

findings.title: MAS proposes ban on interest payments on MAS-regulated stablecoins and restricts 'MAS-regulated' label
findings.summary: On 1 September 2026, MAS published a consultation proposing to prohibit interest payments on MAS-regulated stablecoins, require 100% high-quality liquid reserve backing, and restrict use of the 'MAS-regulated' label to licensed issuers only. This follows Singapore's stablecoin licensing framework (2024) and responds to concerns about retail investor risk. The consultation is open to stakeholders. Wealth managers advising clients on digital-asset allocations involving Singapore-regulated stablecoins should monitor compliance implications.
